target_customer: Mac consumers with files scattered across cloud services, web apps and local disks
problem: Personal content is spread across Dropbox, Google Drive, Facebook, Instagram and local files with no single place to find and organize it.
product_category: Cross platform personal content manager (universal finder for the cloud)

founders.name: Jordan Lee
education: Princeton graduate student per alumni article
founders.background_notes: YC page says currently CEO at backer.com and savingforcollege.com.

founders.name: Tony Xiao
founders.background_notes: A Princeton alumni article also names Arman Suleimenov as a developer.

competitors.name: Otixo
competitors.what: Dashboard consolidating Dropbox, Google Drive, S3, Box and others with copy between clouds and WebDAV mapping

competitors.name: Gladinet
competitors.what: Unified namespace over cloud and local storage via drive mapping

technical_complexity.rationale: Native Mac app integrating several cloud and social APIs into a virtual file system; API changes were a constant maintenance burden.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on third party APIs and could be copied or absorbed by Dropbox, Google or Apple.

market_need_then: In 2012 consumers were adopting multiple cloud storage services and social photo apps, creating fragmentation; press launched a Mac public beta in July and August 2012.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as Finder for the cloud, referencing Apple's Finder

brand_strength.rationale: Generic dictionary word, no evidence of brand press beyond launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: Collections launched a Mac public beta in mid 2012 and joined YC Summer 2012 as a two person team. No funding, acquisition or shutdown announcement was found, and the cause of its becoming inactive is not public. Its dependency on third party cloud APIs and a crowded field of aggregators and giants suggest a hard path, but this is inference, not a sourced cause.
notes: No company website is listed in the directory data, so the site is treated as dead and not fetched. Shutdown cause is not public; failure factor competition_won is a weak inference and should be treated as low confidence. No funding found, which is not evidence of no funding. Founder education from a Princeton alumni snippet, not fully verified.
